title: Feralas
body: Feralas is a vast, rain-soaked forest in southwestern Kalimdor, green and wild beside the dry lands around it, and so abruptly does it end at its borders that scholars suspect strange magic was at work. Long ago the night elves built here, and their ruins lie everywhere beneath the canopy, above all the broken city of Eldre'Thalas, now called Dire Maul. Today the Gordunni ogres are the strongest power in the forest. The Alliance holds Feathermoon Stronghold on Sardor Isle, the Horde Camp Mojache in the east.

title: Feathermoon Stronghold
body: Feathermoon Stronghold is the Alliance bastion of Feralas, a night elf fortress on Sardor Isle reached by ferry from the Forgotten Coast. General Shandris Feathermoon led an expedition here and commands it still. It is a place of scholars as much as soldiers: the priestess Vestia Moonspear is one of the most learned minds anywhere, and her husband Latronicus, Shandris's second, deals with the naga who have come ashore to the south.

title: Shandris Feathermoon
body: Shandris Feathermoon is General of the Sentinel Army and commander of Feathermoon Stronghold. Orphaned when the Burning Legion destroyed her village in the War of the Ancients, she was taken in by Tyrande Whisperwind and grew up at her side, through the Sundering and the long ages of the Sentinels, until she rose to lead them. In Feralas she would gladly throw her full strength against the naga, but will not leave her island open to the Horde.

parts.body: She keeps a quieter circle as well: with the druid Quintis Jonespyre she belongs to the Protectorate, colleagues who take a close and private interest in the work done for Fandral Staghelm, and would rather he did not hear of it.

title: Ruins of Solarsal
body: The Ruins of Solarsal, on Sardor Isle south of Feathermoon Stronghold, are far older than any of the night elves' present works, long left in peace by the Sentinels. Now the Hatecrest naga fill them in alarming numbers, their royals commanding from a cave on the Isle of Dread across the water. At the heart of the ruins stands a gazebo that does not belong, newer than the stones around it, banded with unknown glyphs and warm to the touch.

parts.body: A relic Lord Shalzaru dug up on the Isle of Dread belongs neither to the ruins nor to the naga: it is something far more alien, and Vestia Moonspear has set herself to unravel it.

title: Camp Mojache
body: Camp Mojache is the Horde's foothold in Feralas, a tauren camp of hide tents astride a swift stream above Wildwind Lake. Here the elder Talo Thornhoof, a hunter broken by a harpy ambush, tells his stories, the warrior Rok Orhan leads the fight against the ogres, and the troll Witch Doctor Uzer'i studies the spirits of beasts. Woodpaw gnolls press up from the south and the Gordunni hold the valley to the north.

parts.body: Uzer'i seeks the muisek, the spirits of slain creatures, which flee at a violent death to seek revenge; captured, they can be bound into the Horde's weapons.

title: Dire Maul
body: In the heart of Feralas rise the broken walls of Eldre'Thalas, a city of Queen Azshara's Highborne, its great halls now called Dire Maul. Gordok ogres hold the grounds outside, their hyenas prowling among the fallen stones, and in an arena within the walls, the Maul, ogre champions brawl for the crowd. Of the elves who once lived here, travelers say little; the wings of the old city are sealed, and few who go in come out with tales.

title: The Writhing Deep
body: Beyond the Woodpaw camps in southeastern Feralas, the earth is broken into the twisted mounds and tunnels of the Writhing Deep, a hive of the insects known here as the Zukk'ash. Workers, wasps and tunnelers swarm over its slopes, even the ore in its veins comes smeared with ooze, and one among them, Stinglasher, is far larger than its kin and wrapped in an aura the others lack.

parts.body: The hive explains the gnolls' fury: a Woodpaw battle map shows most of their strength turned south against it, a war on two fronts.
sources: quest 4135 description and reward text (Writhing Deep south of the gnoll camps; pod encasing a humanoid)

parts.body: Not every victim dies at once. The Zukk'ash seal some of those they overwhelm in hard, mucous pods large enough to hold a grown elf, paralyzed but alive.

title: Ruins of Isildien
body: Deep in the High Wilderness of southern Feralas lie the Ruins of Isildien, the remains of a large night elf city destroyed long ages ago, where a broad stair climbs to a round hall that may once have been a temple. The Gordunni have made it their stronghold, home to their mightiest battlemasters, warlocks and mage-lords, and their magic seems to wreak havoc on the very ground: across the High Wilderness, the trees wither wherever they dwell.

parts.body: A soiled scroll shows a dark ceremony conducted by the mage-lords, and an orb taken from one of them proves very powerful and very dangerous.

title: Ruins of Ravenwind
body: West of the Dream Bough lie the Ruins of Ravenwind, an ancient night elf city overrun by the Northspring harpies, whose queen, Edana Hatetalon, is said to have a heart of crystal, empty of all but hatred. Older magic lingers among the stones: four flames named Samha, Imbel, Byltan and Lahassa still burn there, and the Equinex Monolith stands silent nearby, keeping whatever it holds.

parts.body: Opened with the Stave of Equinex, charged with the four flames, the monolith gives up a stone hidden with great care: the Morrow Stone, whose purpose no one yet knows.

title: The Dream Bough
body: In the far north of Feralas, Jademir Lake spreads its quiet waters around an island where a towering tree, the Dream Bough, rises above the forest: one of four great trees through which the Emerald Dream touches the waking world, the others standing in Duskwood, the Hinterlands and Ashenvale. The green dragonflight guards it jealously, and few mortals linger.

parts.body: Of late Emeriss, one of the great green dragons of Ysera's flight, emerges here at times, sick with corruption, and turns on any who come near.

title: Thalanaar
body: Thalanaar is a small night elf way-station on the eastern edge of Feralas, where the forest gives way to the dry canyons of the Thousand Needles, with little more than a hippogryph roost and a pair of merchants. The druid Falfindel Waywarder keeps his post here, and couriers from Feathermoon Stronghold cross the whole breadth of Feralas to bring him supplies.
